summary: All four findings confirmed, three of them with a narrowed fix; none rejected. /1 and /2 are right as stated: the continuous-section theorem (TauCeti.exists_continuous_section, _of_le) is built at Tau Ceti f790474, and Weierstrass division and preparation with uniqueness are in Mathlib 082e2d3, so overlaps[0] and overlaps[5] should import them rather than plan or move proofs. /3: the mathematics is right (C2, H=1, F2 gives 4 against 2 elements in degree zero, so no chain isomorphism exists). But the PPG link map never names shapiroCochainIso, all its edges stay valid, and the same defect is already recorded in the partial, unreviewed ProfiniteCohomology link map (gaps[0]). The fix is therefore a supplier note only, and medium rather than high. /4: the arbitrary-procyclic alternative in ProfiniteCohomology §6 is false (C2: H²(C2,F2)=F2). But the proposed PPG Layer 4 → PC4/6/10/11 links fail the §10 test. Ẑ is Mathlib's ProfiniteGrp.profiniteCompletion of ℤ, with lift, lift_unique and homEquiv, which PC consumes directly within its declared dependency boundary. PPG Layer 4's stated outputs (maximal pro-p quotient ≅ ℤ_p, Sylow characterization) are not used by those examples. So no links are added; the fix is a supplier-correction note only. The proposed edges would be acyclic (checked), but they are not dependencies.

findings.reason: Confirmed at Tau Ceti f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369. Section.lean:253 exists_continuous_section_of_le gives the section of G ⧸ K → G ⧸ H for K ≤ H, H closed, normalized at the identity coset. Both proofs are complete (no sorry or axiom in the file). Both names are in the pinned declarations index. A finite subgroup of a profinite (Hausdorff) group is closed, so PPG Layer 5's finite-kernel milestone is the special case K = 1, H = N. AUDIT-22 (accepted) already classifies that PPG Layer 5 target as 'tauceti', fit 'more general'. The ProfiniteCohomology STATUS page (dated 2026-09-01) still says the section is missing, so the overlap author was working from stale status. The error in the map is the last two sentences of overlaps[0].proposal. They invite moving the elementary finite-kernel proof into PC Layer 0, which would re-prove a built theorem, and nowhere in the overlap is the existing declaration named. PMIA:L4's atlas text says 'Prove Weierstrass division and preparation for O[[T]], including continuity and uniqueness'. overlaps[5] endorses that ('L4 proves Weierstrass division and preparation for O[[T]]'; 'PMIA proves its broader O-coefficient theorems'), so the map's recommendation plans an existing Mathlib theorem again. One correction to the finding's evidence: 'the complete-DVR O case is an instance' holds for the concrete rings, through the instances IsAdicComplete 𝓂[K] 𝒪[K] (NumberTheory/LocalField/Basic.lean:176) and IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal ℤ_[p]) ℤ_[p] (Padics/PadicIntegers.lean:539). The mathematics is right, and I re-derived it. homogeneousCochains X is the G-invariants of resolution'X X n = resolutionX X (n+1), so degree 0 is C(G, X)^G ≅ X. For G = C2, H = 1, A = F2: the G side in degree 0 is Coind_1^G F2 = Map(C2, F2), with 4 elements. The H side is C(1, F2)^1 ≅ F2, with 2 elements. An independent enumeration of the equivariant maps gives 4 against 2. So the 'chain isomorphism shapiroCochainIso between the two canonical homogeneous-cochain complexes' in ProfiniteCohomology Layer 10 cannot exist, although cohomological Shapiro holds. The finding's framing and severity are wrong, however. (a) The PPG link map never names shapiroCochainIso. links[11] and links[32] cite shapiroIso, dimensionShiftIso, corestriction_comp_res and longExact_exact, which are all true statements on cohomology, so the map states nothing false and no edge changes. (b) The same defect with the same counterexample is already recorded in the ProfiniteCohomology link map (research/blueprint/links/tauceti_TauCetiRoadmap_ProfiniteCohomology.json, gaps[0], 'Shapiro complex-level contract needs clarification') and its handoff note. The finding does not mention this, although it says it compared all link packets touching PPG. That map is status 'partial' and unreviewed, so the defect is not yet in any accepted deliverable, and a cross-reference from this accepted map is worth one sentence. Severity medium, not high. Authorized scope: retain links[11] and links[32] and their evidence unchanged. Add one supplier note, either to the ProfiniteCohomology examined note or as a top-level 'requests' entry addressed to the ProfiniteCohomology maintainer. The note says: Layer 10's shapiroCochainIso cannot be a degreewise isomorphism of the canonical complexes (C2, H=1, F2); replace it by a named chain map proved a quasi-isomorphism (or a homotopy equivalence), with shapiroIso induced on cohomology; this map's consumers use only shapiroIso, dimensionShiftIso and coindAcyclic; it cross-references the ProfiniteCohomology link map's gaps[0]. Do not add a PPG-local Shapiro, change any consumer statement or edit the upstream README.

Confirmed only for its supplier-document error. The four proposed links are rejected. Correct: ProfiniteCohomology §6 (the 'Hⁱ(Ẑ, -) and cd_p Ẑ = 1' example, Layers 4, 6, 10, 11) allows 'state the example over an arbitrary procyclic group with a topological generator', and that alternative is false. C2 is procyclic, and H²(C2, F2) = F2: I re-enumerated 2 normalized cocycles and 1 normalized coboundary. ℤ_p is another counterexample, since cd_ℓ ℤ_p = 0 for ℓ ≠ p, against 'cd_p Ẑ = 1 for every p'. This is recorded nowhere else in the repository. Not correct: the missing-link claim. (i) PPG Layer 4's stated outputs are the rank-one chain maximalProPQuotient p (profiniteCompletion ℤ) ≅ lim ℤ/p^n ≅ ℤ_p, freeProP p (Fin 1) ≅ ℤ_p and the Sylow characterization in Ẑ. The PC examples (H¹(Ẑ, ℤ/n) ≅ ℤ/n, H²(Ẑ, M) = 0 for torsion M, H²(Ẑ, ℤ) ≅ ℚ/ℤ, cd_p Ẑ = 1, cor ∘ res on nẐ) use none of them, so the 'exact match' test of PROTOCOL §10 for an inferred link fails. Shared vocabulary (Ẑ) is not a dependency. (ii) The carrier is Mathlib's ProfiniteGrp.profiniteCompletion applied to ℤ, which PPG itself consumes (Layer 0, 'Consume ProfiniteGrp.ProfiniteCompletion'), with ProfiniteCompletion.lift, lift_unique and homEquiv at 082e2d3. PC's option 'Build Ẑ as the profinite completion of ℤ' is therefore the same object, not a second construction, and it stays inside PC's declared dependency boundary (only InductionRestriction), which this map's ProfiniteCohomology examined note records. (iii) A minor misstatement: links 19 and 21 come from PPG Layer 3; the Layer 4 links are 20 and 22. The proposed PPG4 → PC4/PC6/PC10/PC11 edges (and PPG0 → the same) would be acyclic: I checked against the 3,508 atlas stageEdges together with every link map in research/blueprint/links (4,213 distinct edges, no non-trivial strongly connected component). Acyclicity does not make them dependencies. Severity medium, not high. Authorized scope: add no links. Add one supplier-correction note, either in the ProfiniteCohomology examined note or as a 'requests' entry addressed to the ProfiniteCohomology maintainer. The note says: delete the arbitrary-procyclic alternative from §6 (counterexample C2, or ℤ_p for ℓ ≠ p), and state the example for Ẑ = ProfiniteGrp.profiniteCompletion of ℤ with Mathlib's universal property, or for a group given with an explicit isomorphism to it. Do not assign Ẑ to a new owner, create a ring-of-profinite-integers task or edit the upstream README.
